scenarios.name: raw-entry-bytes-1985
scenarios.why: a caller with no typed layout passes 1985 bytes as the LINK COMMAREA (X10, #7954): a valid 99-byte UPDACC record, then a tail; the area is longer than DFHCOMMAREA's 1985-byte storage when over 1985, so the bytes past it travel in `beyond` and come back

scenarios.name: raw-entry-direct-1985
scenarios.why: the same 1985 bytes by direct entry (X10, #7954)

scenarios.name: entry-only-1985
scenarios.why: #7954 slice 19: the same 1985 bytes with no link area (entry_only): the byte[] entry copy fills DFHCOMMAREA and its tail past 1985 is `beyond`

scenarios.name: short-calen-98
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 98, shorter than the 99-byte COMMAREA layout: the port truncates its storage to the area the caller passed and restores it afterwards; a scenario after it checks the restore (#7954)

notes: CBSA's update-account service (UPDACC, LINKed with the UPDACC copybook's COMMAREA): the account is read by the program's own sort code (987654) and COMM-ACCNO with a SELECT INTO from Db2 table ACCOUNT (unqualified: the bind's QUALIFIER, IBMUSER); a failed SELECT (+100, -305 ...) or an account type that is blank or starts with a space gives COMM-SUCCESS 'N' and no UPDATE; otherwise ACCOUNT_TYPE, ACCOUNT_INTEREST_RATE and ACCOUNT_OVERDRAFT_LIMIT are UPDATEd, and the COMMAREA is refilled from the host variables, each date reformatted from Db2's character form (YYYY-MM-DD) to DDMMYYYY. The table is compared after every scenario.
